Anya: Heads-up — just brought kumori-v2 (int8) into staging and seeing a locale-specific regression for mixed KO+ZH inputs. BLEU down ~6 pts on the ko-zh devset, failing a few integration tests. Reproducer attached.

eval-bot: REGRESSION_SUMMARY: model=kumori-v2-int8 metric=BLEU delta=-6.2 dataset=ko_zh_mixed_dev id=RG-2026-311

Sasha: Can you paste a couple of concrete examples? Need to see tokenization diffs, not only BLEU.

Anya: sure — quick excerpt (input -> expected -> kumori-v2-int8 output):
```
input: "서울역에서 北京行 버스가 멈췄다"
expected: "버스가 서울역에서 北京(북경)으로 출발했다."  # ok from float16 baseline
int8_out: "버스가 서울역에서 京으로 출발했다."        # lost han char grouping
```
Token id snapshots (baseline float16 vs int8):
```
before_token_ids: [1342, 9001, 2345, 7810]
after_token_ids:  [1342, 9001, 2350, 7810]
```
So the han ideograph got mapped to a different subtoken boundary.

Kevin: That looks like a tokenizer ID shift, possibly from vocab remap or a new subtoken merge. Did we change tokenizer mapping during quantization step or apply a different vocab table at compile time?

Anya: We pinned the tokenizer artifact to the repo's main build (sha: a1b2c3). The quant pipeline uses the serialization path from the int8 converter which includes a small byte-level remap step. I suspect the remap.

Lia: Two hypotheses: (1) quant conversion emitted a different token-table ordering (2) runtime kernel for int8 path uses a fallback preprocess that normalizes ZWJ/ZWSP differently. Any logs from the converter?

Anya: Converter log snippets:
```
[2026-02-11 08:12:03] serialize_vocab remap_table_entries=3
[2026-02-11 08:12:03] applied_remap {old:2345,new:2350}
```
We didn't expect remap_table_entries > 0 for this model.

Sasha: Oof. Could be intentional (collision avoidance) or accidental bug in remap heuristics. @Kevin can you bisect the converter commits 2026-02-01..2026-02-12? If it's in the serializer, we should revert until we understand.

Kevin: I'll start a bisect now. Command I'll run:
```
./tools/quant_bisect --model kumori-v2 --from 2026-02-01 --to 2026-02-12 --repro tests/fixtures/ko_zh_mixed.txt
```
Assigning to me.

Tori: In parallel, can we add a smoke eval to the staging gating that checks token-id stability for mixed-script sentences? If remap happens silently we need an alert.

Anya: Good call — added a todo in PR: add a token-stability test with 10 mixed examples. I'll open the PR once Kevin confirms the offending commit.

Kevin: Bisect started. First pass shows converter@2026-02-09 reproduces the remap. Narrowing.

Lia: If bisect lands in serializer heuristics, we should prefer deterministic remap ordering or preserve original vocab indices when possible. Changing remap could break cached checkpoints.

Anya: For immediate mitigation we can pin staging to kumori-v2-fp16 and block the int8 rollout. I've applied a canary rule: int8=false for channel=staging.

Sasha: +1. Also add a note to the release ticket and spike an eval-run for other locales (zh-jp, ja-kr) to ensure this remap isn't broad.
